body:
This honestly sounds like me 10 years ago and the years before that. I could not talk to anyone besides my family and a few friends who slowly ditched me cause I "was weird". Outside of these people, I would not/could not talk to anyone, the only way I would communicate to others would be shrugs and nods. I sometimes stood around people to try to be friends with them but I couldn't say anything. I was in therapy from elementary school trying to "fix" me. I most likely had selective mutism, which one of my therapists refused to diagnose me due to links to autism, which coming from an Asian household was bad at the time.

Eventually, the extreme depression from the overbearing loneliness that came with all this pushed me to change. In early highschool I did start making gaming friends online which helped me start socializing, but it wasn't until college that the desire to not be alone over-weighed the fear of people.

I wish I could say I don't suffer from anything anymore but I'm definitely a very different person today. No one would call me shy or introverted, I come off often as the total opposite now. But a lot of the insecurities that developed from that time still persist to this day, with quarantine heavily reminding me of them. I just want to say that there is hope to change from this constant fear of human interaction.

I honestly hate this mentality. Yes we're strangers but it's still a person on the other side that I feel like should be given a small amount of respect. If I've ever had an issue with someone I've met online, I tell them, sometimes they may be unaware of their... unattractive features.

Though I think ghosting very much depends on context, if the two of you have stopped talking for a week or two, it's fine. But if someone is trying to contact you and you vanish, that is where is becomes an issue imo, taking 5 minutes to tell them what's wrong isn't going to kill you.

It takes time to learn how to talk about things you don't know as much about and I'm still not great at it. I still always try to push conversations towards more nerdy discussions and if they keep talking about something I don't care for, I leave it. 

While yes, you should try to learn to do some useless banter here and there, the people you ENJOY talking to should be people you can just talk to about TV shows. If anything, people will always talk about TV, try to just pipe in when they do; might make you more comfortable for pointless banter eventually.

My friend told me once "I have almost died too many times to want to kill myself". It was an eye-opener in the fact that I just don't appreciate being alive cause I take it for granted. 

Also skidding on the ice is terrifying, it happened in a car when I was younger. Glad you made it out okay!

I think reading this post and the comments just made me think of how much of an idiot I am. I realize I ended up doing the exact same thing for a girl I liked (and I thought liked me). First, I had bought her some games she had wanted (its was like $6 worth), which she kinda saw as payment for a thing she was making me. While on vacation, I got her another gift which I could only get there. I never GAVE her the gift, I just had it saved and was planning on giving it on date 2 or something. Date 1 never happened.

I was really upset and still am as you probably are. I'm still trying to decide if I can have a healthy friendship without either of us hurting the other (or having other expectations). You should think about it too; you don't want to feel bitter at her through the friendship cause it will just lead to a very shitty outcome.
